subject: Recap & next steps — locale evaluation (EU / APAC)
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Sørensen <anna.sorensen@linguatech.eu>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps — locale evaluation (EU / APAC)

Hi Anna — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope and what we'll deliver for the quick evaluation run: 

Recap (what you told us):
- Primary business need: automated multilingual product descriptions and content normalization for Nordic + DACH markets (primary) and beta support for JP/TH in APAC.
- Pain: current vendor has regressions on diacritics and locale-specific brand phrases; latency target is <= 300ms p95 per generate call for short descriptions (<= 120 tokens).
- Data: you can share ~5k labeled examples (source text + target localized copy) for initial eval — you mentioned some PII concerns, see below.

Proposed quick evaluation deliverables (1-week sprint):
1) Run token-level and quality evals across recommended model variants for the languages below (EN-NO, SV, DA, DE-DE, DE-AT, FR-FR, NB, JP, TH).
2) Provide per-language precision/recall-style metrics (BLEU, chrF, and our Redwood locale score) + latency/cost estimates.
3) Share prompt set we used and the raw evaluation artifacts so your engineers can re-run locally.

What we need from you to start:
- Confirm final target languages (list + priority).
- Upload the sample set (CSV) to the shared drive link or send as attachment (5k rows ideal; we can work with fewer).
- Confirm whether samples contain PII that needs redaction or if LinguaTech will pre-redact.
- Any regulatory requirements (EU data residency, DPA clauses) beyond standard GDPR.

Next steps / timeline:
- If you can drop the sample set today, we’ll schedule an internal run and share results by EOD Friday (Aug 28).
- I'll loop in Lauren from Applied ML to propose model variants and evaluation config.

Attachments: redwood_eval_plan_v1.pdf (brief plan + eval config).

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0129

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — locale evaluation (EU / APAC)

Hi Vivek — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few items and attaching the sample set (lingua_locale_sample_set_v2.csv). A couple notes from our side:

- Final language list (priority order): NO, SV, DA, DE (DE-DE + DE-AT), FR, EN (fallback), JP (pilot), TH (pilot).
- Samples: ~3.2k rows, some rows include user-submitted product names (may be considered PII by our privacy team). We can either flag those columns or send a redacted export — which do you prefer for the eval?
- Latency: our internal SLA for user-facing generation is 300ms p95, same as you captured, but we can tolerate 500ms p95 for JP/TH during the pilot phase.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Which model family would you recommend for a balance of cost and locale quality for Nordic + DACH?
2) Do you have prior benchmark PDFs for EU languages we can review (ideally with token-level cost estimates)?
3) Any specific prompt patterns you plan to test for brand-preserving generation?

I’ve attached the sample CSV and a short internal note (it@linguatech.eu) about our data handling constraints.

Attachments: lingua_locale_sample_set_v2.csv (3.2k rows, CSV)

Best,
Anna
Head of Product, LinguaTech AS
anna.sorensen@linguatech.eu | +47 22 33 44 55
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Sørensen <anna.sorensen@linguatech.eu>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — locale evaluation (EU / APAC)

Hi Anna — welcome, and thanks for the sample. Quick answers and the run plan we’ll execute once you confirm redaction preference.

Model recommendations (initial sweep):
- Efficiency / cost-conscious: redwood-mistral-13b-q4 (good for short-form content, strong token efficiency).
- Quality / locale-sensitive: redwood-locale-xxl (13–20B class, trimmed attention patterns for diacritics) and redwood-locale-xxl-quant (quantized variant we use for Dedicated to cut token cost).
- Fallback / highest-quality for tricky JP/TH: redwood-asia-xxl (larger decoder with improved tokenization for CJK & SEA scripts).

Evaluation plan (what we’ll run):
- Metrics: BLEU, chrF, REDWOOD_LOCALE_SCORE (our internal composite), and per-example human-like tag failures.
- Prompt sets: 1) brand-preserve-short (short instruction + brand token constraints), 2) descriptive-template (structured template with product attributes), 3) neutralize-for-seo (SEO-friendly rewrite). We’ll attach the prompt JSONs to the results.
- Perf config: max_tokens=120, concurrency=8, batch_size=16, sampling: top_p=0.9 / temp=0.2 for production-like output.
- Latency measurement: 100 warmup requests + 1k instrumentation requests per language to capture p50/p95/p99.

Links/benchmarks we’ll reference:
- Redwood locale eval summary: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/locale-eval-2026
- Prompt sets & run harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cEvalSets

Action items (for LinguaTech):
- Please confirm redaction preference (we can accept flagged PII column or a pre-redacted file) — if flagged, specify columns.
- Confirm target languages list (Anna, the list you sent looks good).

I’ll kick off the eval as soon as we have the final CSV and redaction decision. If results show language-specific regressions we’ll propose targeted fine-tune / prompt engineering tests and a small canary rollout plan for Dedicated capacity in eu-west region.

Attachments: prompt_sets_brand_preserve.json (will post to drive), eval_harness_instructions.md

—
Lauren Bishop
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Quick note from security/compliance:
- If LinguaTech opts for flagged PII (we get raw values), we need a signed DPA and confirmation of storage region; prefer EU-only storage for the artifacts and logs from this eval.
- Please upload any SOC2/infosec questionnaires to our secure collection link instead of email. (I’ve attached the SOC2 evidence stub and our onboarding checklist to the drive link.)
- From a quality-regression standpoint: request that we include a small holdout of previously published localized text (100–200 rows) so we can detect regressions vs your production baseline before recommending rollout.

CC-ing Anna so she sees the compliance ask. Vivek — can you get LinguaTech to sign the DPA and drop files into the drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cEvalSets ? Once DPA is in place we’ll run the eval in eu-west and provide per-language artifacts.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
